title: Topos adjunction for a continuous cocontinuous functor
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites and let $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ denote their categories of sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3) and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1); no local fullness, local faithfulness or cover-density is assumed. Define $L\mathcal G(U)=\mathcal G(u(U))$, with restriction maps induced by $u$. For a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal C$ define $R\mathcal F(V)$ to be the set of families $(s_{A,\psi})$, indexed by all pairs $(A,\psi:u(A)\to V)$, with $s_{A,\psi}\in\mathcal F(A)$ and $\mathcal F(a)(s_{A,\psi})=s_{B,\psi\circ u(a)}$ for every $a:B\to A$. Restriction along $h:V'\to V$ sends this family to $(s_{A,h\circ\psi'})_{A,\psi':u(A)\to V'}$; maps of sheaves act componentwise. Then $L$ and $R$ are functors between the sheaf categories, and $L\dashv R$ is the adjunction of the morphism of topoi $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ associated to the cocontinuous functor $u$: $g^{-1}=L$, $g_*=R$. In particular $L$ preserves finite limits. Its counit at $\mathcal F$, evaluated at $U$, is $(s_{A,\psi})\mapsto s_{U,\mathrm{id}_{u(U)}}$, and its unit at $\mathcal G$, evaluated at $V$, is $t\mapsto (\mathcal G(\psi)(t))_{A,\psi}$. A morphism of topoi here means an adjoint pair whose left adjoint preserves finite limits.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf], continuity implies that $L\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ u$ is a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$ for every sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal D$. Composition with $u$ sends a natural transformation to its components at $u(U)$ and respects identities and composition. Thus $L:\Sh(\mathcal D)\to\Sh(\mathcal C)$ is the stated functor.

For each $V$, the pairs $(A,\psi:u(A)\to V)$ form a set because both sites are small [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). Hence $R\mathcal F(V)$ is the subset of $\prod_{(A,\psi)}\mathcal F(A)$ cut out by the displayed compatibility equations; it is a set, including when the indexing set is empty. Restriction along $h:V'\to V$ replaces $\psi'$ by $h\psi'$; the equation $h\psi'u(a)=(h\psi')u(a)$ shows that compatibility is preserved. Replacing indices successively along $h$ and $k$ equals replacing them along $hk$, and identity replacement changes nothing. A natural transformation $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ sends every compatible family to a compatible family by naturality and commutes with these restrictions. Thus the formula gives a presheaf and a functor on presheaves.

source.place: Section Tag 00XF (section-more-functoriality-PSh), compatible-family formula and restriction maps

proof.text: We first prove separatedness of $R\mathcal F$ for a sheaf $\mathcal F$. Let $\{h_j:V_j\to V\}$ be a covering and let $s,s'\in R\mathcal F(V)$ have equal restrictions to each $V_j$. Fix $(A,\psi)$. Base change of this covering along $\psi:u(A)\to V$ is a covering of $u(A)$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). Cocontinuity [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1) supplies a covering $\{f_i:A_i\to A\}$ and arrows $\theta_i:u(A_i)\to V_{j(i)}$ with $h_{j(i)}\theta_i=\psi u(f_i)$. Compatibility and the assumed equality give $\mathcal F(f_i)(s_{A,\psi})=s_{A_i,h_{j(i)}\theta_i}=s'_{A_i,h_{j(i)}\theta_i}=\mathcal F(f_i)(s'_{A,\psi})$. The injectivity part of the sheaf equalizer for $\mathcal F$ gives $s_{A,\psi}=s'_{A,\psi}$. This holds for every coordinate, hence $s=s'$.

source.place: Tag 00XK (lemma-pu-sheaf), covering-lifting paragraph, written directly on compatible families

proof.text: Now let $t^j\in R\mathcal F(V_j)$ be a matching family for the same covering. For each $(A,\psi)$ choose a covering and lifts $f_i,\theta_i$ as in step 3, and put $x_i=t^{j(i)}_{A_i,\theta_i}\in\mathcal F(A_i)$. On $P=A_i\times_A A_k$, which exists by the covering-base-change axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), the maps $\theta_i u(\operatorname{pr}_1)$ and $\theta_k u(\operatorname{pr}_2)$ have the same composite to $V$: both are $\psi u(f_i\operatorname{pr}_1)=\psi u(f_k\operatorname{pr}_2)$. The universal property gives a map $u(P)\to V_{j(i)}\times_V V_{j(k)}$; this target exists by the site axiom on $\mathcal D$. Evaluate the matching equality of $t^{j(i)}$ and $t^{j(k)}$ on this pair. Their family-compatibility equations identify the resulting two sections of $\mathcal F(P)$ with $\mathcal F(\operatorname{pr}_1)(x_i)$ and $\mathcal F(\operatorname{pr}_2)(x_k)$. Thus the $x_i$ match, and the existence part of the sheaf equalizer gives a unique $x_{A,\psi}\in\mathcal F(A)$ restricting to them. No preservation of these overlaps by $u$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 00XK (lemma-pu-sheaf), covering-lifting and overlap paragraphs; direct componentwise gluing

proof.text: The section $x_{A,\psi}$ does not depend on the cover or the lifts. Given a second choice $\{f'_k:A'_k\to A,\theta'_k\}$, the objects $P_{ik}=A_i\times_A A'_k$ form a common covering of $A$: first base change the second cover to each $A_i$, then compose coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). Write $p:P_{ik}\to A_i$ and $p\prime:P_{ik}\to A\prime_k$ for the projections, and $z,z\prime\in\mathcal F(A)$ for the sections glued from the two choices. The maps $\theta_i u(p)$ and $\theta\prime_k u(p\prime)$ have equal composites to $V$, so they determine $\rho:u(P_{ik})\to W=V_{j(i)}\times_V V_{j\prime(k)}$, with projections $r:W\to V_{j(i)}$ and $r\prime:W\to V_{j\prime(k)}$. The matching equality $R\mathcal F(r)(t^{j(i)})=R\mathcal F(r\prime)(t^{j\prime(k)})$ evaluated at $(P_{ik},\rho)$ gives $t^{j(i)}_{P_{ik},\theta_i u(p)}=t^{j\prime(k)}_{P_{ik},\theta\prime_k u(p\prime)}$. Family compatibility and the defining restrictions of $z,z\prime$ identify these with $\mathcal F(f_i p)(z)$ and $\mathcal F(f\prime_k p\prime)(z\prime)$; the maps $f_i p=f\prime_k p\prime$ are equal. Injectivity of the sheaf equalizer on this common covering gives their equality. This argument applies to any covering of $A$ equipped with such factorizations, not only to the one first obtained by cocontinuity.

source.place: Tag 00XK (lemma-pu-sheaf), final overlap paragraph, with independence of the local lifts spelled out

proof.text: For $a:B\to A$, base change the cover $\{f_i:A_i\to A\}$ of step 4 to $B$, with $q_i:B\times_A A_i\to B$ and $p_i:B\times_A A_i\to A_i$. The maps $\theta_i u(p_i)$ factor $\psi u(aq_i)$ through $V_{j(i)}$. The section assigned to this lifted cover is $\mathcal F(a)(x_{A,\psi})$: its restriction along $q_i$ is $\mathcal F(p_i)(x_i)=t^{j(i)}_{B\times_A A_i,\theta_i u(p_i)}$, by compatibility of $t^{j(i)}$. Independence in step 5 therefore gives $\mathcal F(a)(x_{A,\psi})=x_{B,\psi u(a)}$. Thus $x=(x_{A,\psi})$ belongs to $R\mathcal F(V)$. For $(A,\theta:u(A)\to V_j)$ the identity cover of $A$ with lift $\theta$ is an allowed factored cover for $(A,h_j\theta)$; step 5 implies $x_{A,h_j\theta}=t^j_{A,\theta}$. So $x$ restricts to $t^j$ for each $j$, and is unique by step 3. This proves the sheaf equalizer condition for $R\mathcal F$. Consequently the componentwise functor of step 2 restricts to $R:\Sh(\mathcal C)\to\Sh(\mathcal D)$. The only site operations used here are identity covers and base change [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1).

source.place: Tag 00XK (lemma-pu-sheaf), conclusion; details of compatible-family descent written out

proof.text: We construct the adjunction bijection explicitly, using the fact that the sheaf categories are full subcategories of presheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). Given $\alpha:L\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$, set $\beta_V(t)=(\alpha_A(\mathcal G(\psi)(t)))_{A,\psi}$. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives the compatibility equation for $a:B\to A$, since $\mathcal F(a)\alpha_A\mathcal G(\psi)=\alpha_B\mathcal G(u(a))\mathcal G(\psi)=\alpha_B\mathcal G(\psi u(a))$. The equation for a restriction $h:V'\to V$ is $\mathcal G(\psi')\mathcal G(h)=\mathcal G(h\psi')$, so $\beta$ is natural. Conversely, given $\beta:\mathcal G\to R\mathcal F$, set $\alpha_A(t)=\beta_{u(A)}(t)_{A,\mathrm{id}}$. Naturality of $\beta$ along $u(a)$ identifies $\beta_{u(B)}(\mathcal G(u(a))(t))_{B,\mathrm{id}}$ with $\beta_{u(A)}(t)_{B,u(a)}$; family compatibility identifies the latter with $\mathcal F(a)(\beta_{u(A)}(t)_{A,\mathrm{id}})$. Hence $\alpha$ is natural. Starting with $\alpha$ and evaluating the constructed $\beta$ at $(A,\mathrm{id})$ recovers $\alpha_A$. Starting with $\beta$, its naturality along $\psi$ gives $\beta_{u(A)}(\mathcal G(\psi)(t))_{A,\mathrm{id}}=\beta_V(t)_{A,\psi}$, so the other composite also recovers the original map. For $c:\mathcal G\prime\to\mathcal G$, naturality of $c$ yields $\alpha_A\mathcal G(\psi)c_V=\alpha_Ac_{u(A)}\mathcal G\prime(\psi)$, so the family associated to $\alpha\circ Lc$ is $\beta\circ c$. For $b:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\prime$, the family associated to $b\circ\alpha$ has coordinate $b_A\alpha_A\mathcal G(\psi)(t)$, which is the coordinate of $Rb\circ\beta$. The inverse bijection has the same naturality since it is inverse to this bijection. They therefore give the bifunctorial hom-set bijection $L\dashv R$, without invoking any Kan-extension or Yoneda theorem as a black box.

source.place: Tag 00XH (lemma-adjoints-pu), adjunction and evaluation description; Tag 00XL (lemma-exact-cocontinuous), restriction to sheaves

proof.text: Apply the bijection of step 7 to the identity of $L\mathcal G$ to obtain the unit: $\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(t)=(\mathcal G(\psi)(t))_{A,\psi}$. Apply its inverse to the identity of $R\mathcal F$ to obtain the counit: $\epsilon_{\mathcal F,U}(s)=s_{U,\mathrm{id}_{u(U)}}$. The composite $\epsilon_{L\mathcal G}\circ L\eta_{\mathcal G}$ at $U$ sends $t\in\mathcal G(u(U))$ to the identity coordinate $\mathcal G(\mathrm{id}_{u(U)})(t)=t$. For the other composite $R\epsilon_{\mathcal F}\circ\eta_{R\mathcal F}$, let $s\in R\mathcal F(V)$. The unit gives at $(A,\psi)$ the family $R\mathcal F(\psi)(s)\in R\mathcal F(u(A))$. Applying $\epsilon_{\mathcal F,A}$ selects its $(A,\mathrm{id})$ coordinate, equal by the restriction formula to $s_{A,\psi}$. Thus both triangle identities hold and the formulas are those claimed.

source.place: Section 00XF and Tag 00XH (lemma-adjoints-pu), projections and evaluation at identity

proof.text: For a finite diagram $M:\mathcal I\to\Sh(\mathcal D)$ with limit cone $\mathcal G$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise](2) says that $\mathcal G(u(U))$, with its projections, is a limit of the sets $M(i)(u(U))$ for every $U$. Since these are precisely $(L\mathcal G)(U)$ and $(LM(i))(U)$, applying clause (2) of the same node on $\mathcal C$ says the cone $L\mathcal G$ is a limit of $LM$. Hence $L$ preserves finite limits (indeed all small limits). The finite indexing category is small, as required by the cited statement; this includes the empty diagram.

source.place: Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf); Tag 00XL (lemma-exact-cocontinuous), left exactness argument; Tag 00XR (lemma-when-shriek)(3)

proof.text: The adjunction of step 7 and finite-limit preservation of step 9 satisfy the stated definition of a morphism of topoi $g:\Sh(\mathcal C)\to\Sh(\mathcal D)$, with $g^{-1}=L$ and $g_*=R$. In the associated cocontinuous construction the inverse image is sheafification of precomposition and the direct image is the compatible-family functor. To identify the former with $L$, use [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: since $L\mathcal G$ is already a sheaf, the identity $L\mathcal G\to L\mathcal G$ has the sheafification universal property. More explicitly the universal map $e:L\mathcal G\to(L\mathcal G)^\#$ has an inverse $r$ induced by the identity, with $re=\mathrm{id}$; uniqueness of factorization gives $er=\mathrm{id}$. These inverse maps are natural by the same uniqueness. Under this canonical identification the hom-set formulas are exactly step 7, and hence give the unit and counit of step 8. Thus this is the morphism associated to $u$, as claimed.
